Title:
Untying Prefill and Decode Loops in Looped Language Models

Authors:
Yang Hu

Primary category: cs.CL (Computation and Language)
Cross-list: cs.LG (Machine Learning)

Comments:
27 pages, 13 figures. Code, per-item results and a script that recomputes every number: https://github.com/yanghu819/untying-prefill-decode

License: CC BY 4.0

Abstract (plain text):
Looped language models run a block of layers several times for every token and use the same number of loops to read the prompt (prefill) and to generate each answer token (decode). Yet generation is almost all decoding: on Ouro-2.6B, prefill takes 0.4-2.8% of the time of a chain-of-thought answer, so extra prefill loops are nearly free. We untie the two loop counts: the prompt is read with m loops and each answer token is decoded with n < m. The released model cannot use the states of a longer prefill, so we distill a small adapter (2.4% of the parameters): LoRA on the decoder when the prefill depth is fixed, or LoopBridge, which adds per-loop key and value maps so that one adapter serves every prefill and decode depth. On Ouro-2.6B with one decode loop, four prefill loops raise the average over 11 benchmarks from 44.2 for the original model to 57.1 (56.8 with LoopBridge), above the original model distilled to one loop on the same data (49.8), and in the same measured time per request they are 14-15 points more accurate than the original model. The gain levels off at two to four prefill loops, and it holds on Ouro-1.4B, on the Thinking models and on looped decision models. Code: https://github.com/yanghu819/untying-prefill-decode
